This form must be executed in duplicate when a child is transferred from a reservation to a nonreservation school. The Superintendent of the nonreservation school will retain the original for his files, and the duplicate shall be deposited in the reservation school records. The reservation superintendent should send to the Commissioner of Indian Affairs his certificate as provided by law. All the blanks must be properly filled in every case. If the information called for on any part of the blank is not known, that fact should be stated. No space should be left unfilled. Whether the parents are living or dead, their names must be given. The person who signs the blank as consenting to the transfer should indicate his relation to the applicant by marking out the word "parent," "guardian," or "next of kin," leaving unmarked only the title appropriate to the signer. INDORSEMENTS. The laws relating to the transfer of Indian children from reservations and schools are as follows: That hereafter no Indian child shall be sent from any Indian reservation to a school beyond the State or Territory in which said reservation is situated without the voluntary consent of the father or mother of such child if either of them are living, and if neither of them are living without the voluntary consent of the next of kin of such child. Such consent shall be made before the agent of the reservation, and he shall send to the Commissioner of Indian Affairs his certificate that such consent has been voluntarily given before such child shall be removed from such reservation. And it shall be unlawful for any Indian agent or other employee of the Government to induce, or seek to induce, by withholding rations or by other improper means, the parents or next of kin of any Indian to consent to the removal of any Indian child beyond the limits of any reservation. (28 Stats., p. 906.) Provided, That hereafter no Indian child shall be taken from any school in any State or Territory to a school in any other State against its will or without the written consent of its parents. (29 Stats., p. 348.) That no Indian pupil under the age of fourteen years shall be transported at Government expense to any Indian school beyond the limits of the State or Territory in which the parents of such child reside or of the adjoining State or Territory. (35 Stat. L., 781.) The rules provide that— A pupil who has been regularly enrolled in a nonreservation school must not be taken to any other nonreservation school without the consent of both superintendents and the Commissioner of Indian Affairs, and superintendents will be held to strict accountability for such pupils taken to their schools. An Indian boy or girl 18 years old and over may, without the consent of parents or others, personally sign the application form on its being changed to suit the case; but in all cases where the parents are living they should first be consulted. This form is to be used only in transfers from reservations or Indian schools to nonreservation schools. CASE RECORD. NAME: Annie Moses Sex: Male Tribe: Nez Perce State: Wash. Remarks: Cushman Indian School Tacoma, Wash., May 26, 1919 Mr. Joe Moses c/o Superintendent Nespelem, Wash. My dear Mr. Moses: I am sending you a letter written to Nancy by the husband of Mary Pecotus. I do not believe this is the right kind of a letter for a girl to receive from a married man and I am returning it to you without Nancy's having seen it, with the suggestion that it would be advisable that Nancy was properly chaperoned during the vacation. Very respectfully, Superintendent. EHH:MG Enc. Cushman Indian School Tacoma, Washington March 21, 1919 Mr. Fred C. Morgan Nespelem, Washington Dear Mr. Morgan: I am returning herewith your letter to Annie Moses pupil at this school, enclosing with it a Sears, Roebuck and Company order which Annie submitted to you. I have talked this matter over with Mrs. Nicholson, the matron and she agrees with me in the belief that Annie does not need the clothing and goods listed thereon. If the parents, however, wish her to have these things, Mrs. Nicholson will be glad to accompany Annie to town for the purpose of purchasing them for her. Very sincerely yours, Superintendent Colville Agency, Nespelem, Wash., March 10, 1919. Miss Annie Moses, Cushman Indian School Tacoma, Washington. Through Superintendent Hammond Dear Friend: I have your letter of March 4th, with an order enclosed for your clothing and other material. I have not seen your father regarding this order but will endeavor to so in the near future. Please take this matter up with your matron and superintendent and, if in their good judgment, you need the clothing and goods listed in your order, a check will be sent to the superintendent covering the purchase. An order of this kind is absolutely unnecessary as you can, in company with the matron, go down town and purchase the articles just as reasonable and doubtless in a much more satisfactory manner than were you to order by mail. I am glad to know that you are getting along well and trust that you will make the best possible use of your time. I am always glad to hear from the boys and girls who are attending Cushman from this reservation. Spring has at last come. The first buttercups made their appearance last Saturday. Your brother Patsy, has gone home to help on the farm. I saw your father Saturday and he said that all your people were well. Very truly your friend, Fred C. Morgan Superintendent VACATION REQUEST FOR PUPIL. We, the undersigned, respectfully request that leave of absence be granted ............................................... ..................................................... Potawatomi Pete Annie Moses from June 15, 1918 to Sept. 5, 1918 to enable her to visit her home. We hereby agree to pay all expenses, including round-trip railroad fares, sleeping-car fares, meals, lodging, stage fares, telegraph and telephone messages, and other incidental expenses connected with the visit. We further agree that said pupil shall be returned to the Cushwa school on or before the last day of the leave of absence. We further agree to deposit with the superintendent of the school sufficient money to defray all expenses to be incurred, and should the pupils, or any one of them, fail to return to school at such time as may be agreed upon by the parents or guardian and the superintendent of the school in which the pupils are enrolled, the amount of money remaining with the superintendent, necessary to the return transportation of the pupil or pupils so neglecting to return, shall be forfeited to the Government; provided, however, that in all cases where it can be shown that there were justifiable reasons for the failure of the return of the pupil the forfeiture of the funds shall not take place. If the pupil neglecting to return is from a reservation, the superintendent of the reservation shall certify to the reasons for the nonreturn of the pupil or pupils. If a pupil's home is not on a reservation, then the certificate of some reputable, disinterested citizen of the community may be requested as to the reasons for the nonreturn of the pupil or pupils. Witnesses: Carley Bob, Date: June 1, 1918 Peter Dan Mother. Guardian. NOTE TO DISBURSING OFFICERS.—All receipts under this agreement must be accounted for officially as Individual Indian Money. However, any forfeitures must be transferred to Miscellaneous Receipts, Class I, and deposited in the Treasury to the credit of the United States. 5-1142 DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR UNITED STATES INDIAN SERVICE Colville Agency, Nespelem, Washington. June 17, 1918 Mr. E. H. Hammond, Supt, Cushman School, Tacoma, Washington. Dear Mr. Hammond: The bearer of this note, Peter Dan Moses, is the father of Annie Moses, one of your pupils from this reservation. He wishes to take his daughter home for the summer vacation and is paying his own way rather than have her make the trip alone. I have written a check against Annie's bank account to cover her expenses returning home and back to school in the fall, and have mailed the check to Mr. Morgan, who is now absent from the agency, for his signature. As soon as this check is received, duly signed, I will immediately send it to you. If arrangements can be made so she can secure her ticket for her passage home before the check arrives I am sure both Annie and her father will greatly appreciate it as he is anxious to return home with his daughter as soon as possible. Yours truly, Fred C. Morgan Superintendent. by Ravel Stearns Clerk. AB 5—297 a COOKING. RECORD CARD—PREVOCATIONAL DIVISION.
